subject: medicine
title: Spondyloarthritis: ankylosing, psoriatic, reactive and enteropathic

steps.tx: Ask about inflammatory **dawn pain** that wakes the patient in the second half of the night and eases with **exercise** but worsens with rest. Ask about alternating buttock ache from sacroiliac disease, prolonged morning **stiffness** that limits bending, red painful eyes in uveitis, heel pain at tendon insertions, sausage digits with psoriasis and nail pits, bloody diarrhoea in bowel disease, and affected relatives.
steps.say: Ask about inflammatory back pain that wakes the patient in the second half of the night and eases with exercise but worsens with rest. Ask about alternating buttock ache from sacroiliac disease, prolonged morning stiffness that limits bending, red painful eyes in uveitis, heel pain at tendon insertions, sausage shaped digits with psoriasis and nail pits, bloody diarrhoea in bowel disease, and relatives with similar disease.

steps.tx: Measure lumbar flexion with the **Schober test** and note limited expansion, then measure the **occiput wall** gap and chest expansion for kyphosis and fibrosis. Press the sacroiliac joints and run FABER testing, feel the Achilles and plantar **enthesis** for tenderness, and inspect sausage digits, pitting nails and scaly skin. Grade activity with BASDAI, test finger floor distance, lamp the eyes for uveitis, and listen for an aortic diastolic murmur.
steps.say: Measure lumbar flexion with the Schober test and note limited expansion, then measure the gap between head and wall with chest expansion for kyphosis and fibrosis. Press the sacroiliac joints and run FABER testing, feel the Achilles and plantar insertions for tenderness, and inspect sausage digits, pitting nails and scaly skin. Grade activity with BASDAI, test finger floor distance, examine the eyes with a slit lamp for uveitis, and listen for an aortic diastolic murmur.

steps.tx: This photograph demonstrates the modified **Schober test** with skin marks placed above and below the bony pelvis and a tape spanning them. The patient bends fully forward while the examiner reads lumbar expansion, and an increase under five centimetres signals **axial disease**. Practise this bedside skill because **limited expansion** offers easy exam marks and tracks disease activity.
steps.say: Look at this photograph because it demonstrates the modified Schober test for lumbar movement. Skin marks sit above and below the bony pelvis with a tape spanning them while the patient bends fully forward. The examiner reads lumbar expansion, and an increase under five centimetres signals axial disease. Practise this bedside skill because limited expansion offers easy exam marks and tracks disease activity.

steps.tx: Grade sacroiliitis on **pelvic X ray** films and catch early disease with **MRI scans** showing marrow oedema before erosions appear. Support the diagnosis with **HLA B27** testing and family screens, track activity with CRP and ESR, and separate bamboo spine bridging from degenerative spurs. Confirm eye disease on slit lamp review, screen the gut with calprotectin, watch conduction on ECG in aortitis, and separate mechanical, rheumatoid, DISH and infective mimics.
steps.say: Grade sacroiliitis on pelvic X ray films and catch early disease with MRI scans that show marrow swelling before erosions appear. Support the diagnosis with HLA B27 testing and family screens, track activity with CRP and ESR, and separate bamboo spine bridging from degenerative spurs. Confirm eye disease on slit lamp review, screen the gut with calprotectin, watch conduction on ECG in aortitis, and separate mechanical, rheumatoid, DISH and infective mimics.

steps.tx: Start daily **NSAID therapy** to cool dawn pain, add regular **physiotherapy** with posture work, swimming and extension, and step up to biologic drugs that block TNF or interleukin pathways in axial disease. Treat eye flares urgently with steroid drops and dilators, stop smoking to slow fusion, counsel B27 positive families, co treat bowel disease, fix hips late, guard minor trauma that snaps fused spines, and track BASDAI with mobility.
steps.say: Start daily anti inflammatory drugs to cool dawn pain, add regular physiotherapy with posture work, swimming and extension, and step up to biologic drugs that block TNF or interleukin pathways in axial disease. Treat eye flares urgently with steroid drops and dilators, stop smoking to slow fusion, counsel families about inherited risk, co treat bowel disease, fix damaged hips late, guard minor trauma that snaps fused spines, and track BASDAI with mobility.
